summary: Architect design of TOL_SCALE authority/test and the exact host-fact matrix (G6), with adversarial review rounds

d1.summary:
Wrote the Architect design document. It has four parts: A) TOL_SCALE authority and test design, B) host-fact matrix, C) G6 implication review, D) instrument specifications. I chose no TOL_SCALE value.

Part A:
- TOL_SCALE is one of the eight layer-2 slots. It bounds ENTITY_INSERT.scaleX/Y/Z per component: absolute, dimensionless, never Euclidean, never relative.
- The decision rule has three branches. R1 is EXACT (zero, or route scale to EXACT_DOUBLE). R2 is a bounded noise floor (margin M, set by the Architect after the evidence) under a ceiling TOL_LENGTH/E_max. R3 is UNUSABLE, and then TOL_SCALE stays UNSET.
- The Architect decides the value after a pre-registration entry; the Coordinator verifies the text.
- The host test is a 147-row probe, defined by bit patterns, with one execution (EVIDENCE_REPETITION = 1, not a statistical count).
- Results are PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN / INVALID, with no automatic retry. The doc also gives a JSON Schema (validated on a generated 147-row sample), 11 failure modes, the "record" semantics, the BA-08 / BA-05 / BA-04 relink flow and the fail-closed fallback.

Findings from grounding the design in the code and documents:
- The contract has a second consumer of the same declared scale tolerance: the SL-4 acceptance (V2.1 15.6; BA-06 C-146).
- Product code already supplies 1e-9 as the scale tolerance in the I-55 reader (RackProjectionSnapshotReader.cs:26-27). BA-08 V7 does not cite this. I treat it as a precedent only.
- BA-05 has no slot-unit vector for scale.
- 138 of the 437 BA-04 V7 scenarios are blocked by K-3 (checked by script).
- BA-05's own census procedure already needs scratch-database references.
- The existing G3A probe is not read-only (AddOverrule).

Part B: the matrix has rows HF-M1..M11, HF-C1..C5, HF-G1..G4, HF-T1..T2 and HF-F1..F3. The six PARAM-05 strings are fixed as A1-R1..R6 (UBR included; MachineGuid read in the 64-bit view). MACHINE_CLASS and SESSION_BUILD_TUPLE are defined separately. G6 was not stretched:
- The RB-range round trip (HF-G2) is flagged NEEDS-OWNER, with a no-write fallback (BA-05 keeps only the ranges that were actually observed).
- The equal-to-style write-back (HF-C4) rests on the Coordinator's earlier ruling (section 236 R-3), not on G6.
- A five-question boundary test is included for auditors.

Part C: G6 changes the host package as follows. H3 splits into a write-back probe and the read-only G6 facts. The host-type facts expressly required by BA-05 V5 are limited to the context-variable types and the RB ranges (read-only). The doc lists what G6 does not authorize and the scope-creep controls.

Part D: nine instruments I-0..I-9, in two DLL classes, R0 (strict read-only) and RS (read-only on product data, writes only to side databases). The doc covers the proposed folder, managed .NET via NETLOAD, TRUSTEDPATHS / SECURELOAD handling, hash pinning, how a reviewer verifies read-only, and the tests that need no AutoCAD versus host-only checks.

The doc ends with 12 Coordinator rulings (R-A..R-L), the residual open questions, the status block and the state lines.

Citations: every cited file has its blob id in section 9, all produced by git hash-object. I checked line citations by reading the cited lines. src/ is identical to main, and no file under src/, tests/ or eng/ was touched. Only the new doc was added (untracked).

AutoCAD and Windows facts that no repository file establishes are tagged [HOST-TO-CONFIRM]; the raw output on the host governs.

R-C: should the comparator and the SL-4 acceptance (V2.1 15.6; BA-06 C-146) share one TOL_SCALE slot or be split? What is the status of the I-55 1e-9 precedent for ST-7?

R-E: for the RB ranges that existing library data cannot cover (HF-G2), does the Owner extend G6 to a scratch round trip, or does BA-05 take the no-write fallback and keep only the ranges actually observed?
R-F: choose the TRUSTEDPATHS option. The Architect recommends one recursive trusted root, set before the six PARAM-05 strings are read.
R-H: are the exact reads A1-R1..R6 accepted for BA-10 V9, including UBR in the OS build (so every cumulative update changes the machine-class label)?

E_max (needed for the ceiling TOL_LENGTH/E_max) and tau_arith depend on fixture plan parameters and on SL-4 / mu_k formulas that are not implemented yet. R1 (EXACT) therefore rests on an assumption (the writer copies the scale bit for bit) that is not yet proven.
Package v2 and AR10-07 are not written; this document supplies their sections 2 and 5.

Some Windows and AutoCAD read commands are Architect knowledge, not repository facts. Examples: (vlax-product-key), the registry value names, getvar behaviour, and NETLOAD under SECURELOAD. They stay tagged [HOST-TO-CONFIRM] until the CAD manager's raw outputs exist.

majors: MAJOR-1 (statistic ignores the persisted-file observation point). D_A is defined at OP1 only (section 2.3 table). OP1 is a re-read of the same in-memory side database after commit. OP2 (save, reopen, re-read) is 'recommended ON', is optional in the schema (`op2` not required, `DA_op2` nullable), and enters the PASS condition only 'when ON' (V2). The rule never uses DA_op2. If the governing comparator reads state that has been through a DWG save and reload, an R1 EXACT conclusion from OP1 alone is unsound. If the governing comparator reads only in-memory state, OP2 is not needed. The design asserts neither with a citation (V2.1 15.7 and BA-08 section 11 do not settle it). Required: either D_A = max(OP1, OP2) with OP2 mandatory, or an explicit cited statement that persistence is in-memory only.

MAJOR-2 (Owner scope is decided at the wrong level; the classification is honest in the table but not in the ruling path). The Owner's wording is 'instrumentos de solo lectura' three times: decisions section 237 point 5, point 8 item 5, and section 236 Owner item (d). The Coordinator's own section 236 says that anything exceeding the Owner's authorization 'se devuelve al Owner'. Instruments I-3, I-5 and I-6 write to side databases and I-6 saves a DWG file (OP2), so they are not read-only. The design coins 'READ-ONLY (PRODUCT)' and pre-selects it as its proposal. It makes the Owner referral conditional ('If there is doubt', R-A), and R-A is addressed to the Coordinator. Redefining an Owner word to widen an Owner-bounded gate is a decision for the Owner. The phase-2 hold in R-G is correct, but R-A, R-B and R-G should state that I-3, I-5, I-6 and the HF-C4 write probe stay blocked until the Owner answers, and should not present the term as an Architect definition. HF-C4 rests on the Coordinator's R-3, which admitted a host activity. R-3 did not admit a non-read-only instrument under the Owner's read-only instrument gate.

MAJOR-3 (the C2 consumer, SL-4 acceptance, is bound to a value that is not derived for it). TS-D-03 and R-C keep one slot, with the C1 meaning (noise floor of host storage and arithmetic), and state that C2 'reads the same value'. (a) The reference quantity of C2 is never defined: V2.1:903/915 and BA-06 C-146 say 'scale within the kind's declared tolerance' without saying within tolerance of what (1? the plan's s? |s-1|?). (b) The noise floor is not evidence for a PRE-WRITE acceptance threshold. (c) Branch R1(b) retires the slot and routes scaleX/Y/Z to EXACT_DOUBLE, which leaves 'the kind's declared tolerance' in V2.1 15.6, C-146 and DC-13 with no referent, and the design does not say what replaces it. (d) V17 4.3 / ST-7 / ST-8 / G4 (V17:912, 972) is the original home of the slot. That is C3, which the design excludes. Yet the I-55 reader already integrated in main supplies 1e-9 as the scale tolerance (RackProjectionSnapshotReader.cs:25-27). The design treats this only as a 'precedent' and defers it to residual question 7. Required: define C2 (or split the slot before sealing) and state the R1(b) consequence for C2.

MAJOR-4 (the derivation rule cannot be applied as written, and pre-registration leaves the main free parameter open). The rule needs `tau_arith` and `E_max`. The design itself says (section 7, items 1 and 2) that these depend on SL-4 / mu_k formulas that are not implemented (grep RACKMIRROR src finds nothing) and on fixture plan parameters that are not fixed. Both R1 (tau_arith = 0) and R2 (max(D_A, tau_arith); ceiling TOL_LENGTH/E_max) are therefore undefined today. The pre-registration (TS-D-05) fixes E_max, 'the form of the justification of M' and the R1(a)/(b) preference, but not M or any rule for M. So M (>= 1, chosen after the evidence) stays a post-hoc discretionary factor, which defeats the anti-tuning purpose the section claims (PA-9 discipline). The step order is also unclear: E_max and the tau_arith derivation should be sealed before the host run, not only 'before the raw evidence is opened', and the design does not say that the oracle and writer formulas must be sealed first. Required: fix M (or a closed function of the evidence) in the pre-registration, and list the sealed prerequisites for tau_arith and E_max as a gate of H4 / the decision.
minors: MINOR-1: R2 proposes new SCALE slot-unit vectors in BA-05 and R1(b) proposes re-routing scaleX/Y/Z in BA-05. BA-05 V5 L-2 (line 1199, AR3-17) and BA-08 V7:392 say TOL_SCALE 'is not a gate of BA-05' and that its value and status live only in BA-08. The design does not cite or reconcile this. Reconcile it, and say what a new BA-05 hash does to the BA-05 and BA-08 candidate chain (BA-08 depends on BA-05).

MINOR-2: the boundary test in 3.5 (question 1) defines 'host-type fact' as 'what the host returns or stores', which is wider than the Owner's 'host-type fact'. The read part of HF-C5 (group-code designation of dimension variables, a number-to-variable assignment, not a type) is placed in G6 on that basis, although the status block says 'no G6 fact was stretched'. R-D asks only about the write output of the R-3 probe, not about the read part. Ask for a ruling on the read part, or move it to ROW3 and flag it.

MINOR-3: authority extent versus statistic. TS-D-03 limits the authority to the fixture scales (+1, -1, plan s; fixtures use (1,1,1)), but D_A takes the maximum over all 147 rows, including PF-2 bases 0.5, 2, 25.4 and 1/25.4. This is conservative and fail-closed (it may push to R3), but the design should state how PF-2 enters the rule or whether it is excluded from D_A.

MINOR-4: the evidence is bound to a tuple without RackCad loaded. Governing runs use other tuples (R8 and decisions section 237 point 3: 'la evidencia no se transfiere automáticamente'). FM-8 mentions one tuple, but the design does not state how a value derived on one tuple is applied in the baseline, nor who accepts that transfer. Say so explicitly (a residual-risk disclosure; Owner Act 2 is reserved).

MINOR-5: S1 makes a manually answered load prompt INVALID for P-A. Under SECURELOAD, a prompt is likely ([HOST-TO-CONFIRM]), so the test may be unrunnable. Specify a scripted or pre-trusted route as a precondition.

MINOR-6: the definition of K_pres ('largest ladder level k such that every row at that level and at every coarser level...') is ambiguous. 'Largest k' means the finest level, and the condition requires all coarser levels to be exact. Rephrase it as 'the finest level such that all levels not finer are bit-identical'. R1 uses K_pres = 52 and D_A = 0, which duplicates one condition for the PF-1 rows.

MINOR-7: JSON Schema and procedure consistency. `op2` is not required per row although PASS V2 requires OP2 'when ON'. The `summary` object has no additionalProperties:false while `rows` does. The PASS state is 'decision-eligible' but the result enum mixes verdict and eligibility. In the status block, section 2.4 says Core Console is allowed only if the Coordinator rules, while R-I proposes interactive for everything. Reconcile.

MINOR-8: G-12 lists 'the plan's uniform s' as a possible expected scale, while the fixtures place every source reference at scale (1,1,1) (BA-08 V7:606). The expected set is therefore {+1, -1} (and s = 1). Tighten the wording so no non-unit expected value is implied.

MINOR-9: the design excludes the clone / import / TransformBy paths (FM-9, section 2.4) while saying the SL-4 writer is not designed. The TOL_SCALE decision therefore depends on a writer route that is not yet fixed. Section 2.8 and R-B should state that K-3 cannot close before that route is fixed. The design says this only as 'a new test version'.

majors: G6 boundary stretch on HF-C5 (read part). The matrix (HF-C5, section 3.4 line 523), the status block (line 702) and section 4.1 place the read part of the group-code designation of the dimension variables inside G6. The Owner's G6 covers 'tipos/rangos RB', 'variables de contexto' and 'cualquier otro host-type fact'. A group-code-to-variable designation is a code assignment, not a host type. Package V1 never put it under G6: row G6 is RB ranges and context variables only, and the designation was in row G5 (write part). The Coordinator's section 236 R-3 ruling covers only 'equal-to-style'. The doc admits in the HF-C5 cell that BA-11 row 3 does not name the designation, but still labels the read part G6 and tells the reader 'no G6 fact was stretched' (line 703). The section 3.5 boundary test also redefines 'host-type fact' as 'what the host returns or stores' (question 1), which widens the Owner's wording. Fix: take the read part out of G6, either as a Coordinator ruling request like R-D or by deriving it from the ROW3 census pairs of HF-C3. Drop the 'no G6 fact was stretched' claim, and tighten question 1 to host value types and ranges.

HF-C3 also carries a dual in-gate basis, 'ROW3 (storage, order) and G6 (host types)'. BA-05 V5 section 5 step 2 (line 1180) already requires the '(code, host value type) pairs in host order' in the census itself, which is ROW3. Citing G6 for part of HF-C3 blurs which rows depend on the Owner extension, and the G6 rows are the ones the Coordinator must confirm separately. Fix: give HF-C3 a single basis (ROW3), or state exactly which cell is G6 and why. Combined with the HF-C5 problem, an auditor cannot tell what G6 added, which is the point of the G6 implication review (Part C).
minors: Capture of the six PARAM-05 strings is not fully deterministic. Section 3.2 requires one raw file per attribute holding UTF-8 bytes without BOM, and says 'the AutoLISP route adds exactly one line terminator'. It does not say how a getvar result reaches the file: command-line copy, which can wrap or truncate a long TRUSTEDPATHS, or an AutoLISP open/write-line with a stated encoding. The default AutoLISP file encoding is not necessarily UTF-8, and a Spanish-locale path with accents would then produce different bytes. This also sits uneasily with BA-11 row 1 ('no instrument'). Fix: fix one transfer mechanism and its encoding, with a check of the byte length against the string length.

A1-R3 relies on 'the single mapping rule above' to compare `(vlax-product-key)` with the registry subkey cross-check. No rule is written for that comparison: hive prefix, `SOFTWARE` against `Software` case, WOW6432 view. Section 3.2 also says 'no case folding' for the extracted string. Fix: state the comparison rule (for example a case-insensitive comparison used only for the cross-check, with the extracted string unchanged) and what happens when `(vlax-product-key)` is not of the form `Software\...`. Cross-check 2 (`MachineRegistryProductRootKey`) needs an instrument, which conflicts with ROW1's 'no instrument'; it is optional but should be marked as outside ROW1.

A1-R2 puts UBR in OsVersionBuild, so every Windows cumulative update changes the MC label. BA-10 (2) says 'OS version and build' and the label hashes the 'exact text that the observation read'. A joined four-part string is a derived text, not a read text. The Owner's AR10_03B_READING says that an 'actualización de software' does not automatically change the label. The doc discloses this and asks the Coordinator in R-H. It is faithful only if BA-10 V9 accepts the join, so treat it as a ruling item before the label is computed.

The TB-C-only tuple binding for HF-M1..M6 is weaker than the Owner's 'toda observación ... ligada a build/machine/session tuple exacta'. The row-level binding stops at TB-C. The getvar reads (HF-M4..M6) happen inside an AutoCAD session and should also carry TB-S.
HF-F1 uses the tuple binding code 'TB-F', which is not defined in the conventions table of section 3.1 (TB-C, TB-B, TB-S, TB-L, TB-R).

HF-T2 (existing block-reference scales and optional extents, ROW2) is an extra section of the R0 census instrument I-2, which also carries the G6 facts HF-G1 and HF-C5. Mixing non-G6, optional output into the instrument that carries the strictest read-only G6 facts works against the doc's own scope-creep control (section 4.3). majors: Unfaithful to the Coordinator ruling R-5 (decisions section 236, around I-52.md line 10016) and to package V1 P-0.3 (line 212). Both say the tools are 'finales y cargadas en la linea base de modulos antes de H1' and that an instrument loaded after the baseline is a plugin change. The design never cites or reconciles either. Its R-G phases the instruments (phase 2 = I-3, I-5, I-6 after R-A, so after H1), and P-A step S1 NETLOADs the instrument mid-run after the S0 baseline reads. HF-M9 reads the module baseline 'before any gate instrument', which implies the same thing. The Owner's R8 acceptance (record 237 point 3) names only 'una build RackCad especificamente fijada'. Section 3.3 extends it to 'every instrument' without saying that this is an extension. A later RS DLL also changes TB-B and starts a new tuple, so I-2 and I-4 evidence, the H1 label and the phase-2 evidence would sit on different tuples. This must either be raised as an explicit ruling request or be changed so that the whole R0 and RS instrument set is final and in the baseline before H1.

The TOL_SCALE instrument split is internally inconsistent. Section 2.4 steps S0 to S8 describe one run in which S7, the P-R inventory pass, follows P-A. Section 5.2 assigns P-R to I-2 (the R0 DLL, command CT21DHG_CENSUS_R) and P-A to I-6 (the RS DLL, command CT21DHG_TOLSCALE). R-G puts I-2 in phase 1 and I-6 in phase 2. The tolscale-raw.json schema requires 'inventory' next to 'rows', with ONE tuple.buildTupleDigest and ONE instrument name and sha256. So the record cannot be produced by a single instrument, a single DLL class or a single tuple. The design must say which DLL writes the inventory, or split the record and the schema, and state that both DLLs are declared in the same tuple.

The read-only verification layers in 5.3 are overclaimed. (a) Layer 2 reads member references from the built DLL with System.Reflection.Metadata. `OpenMode.ForWrite` is an enum literal that the C# compiler inlines as an int constant, so it leaves no member reference. `GetObject(id, OpenMode.ForWrite)` is therefore indistinguishable from a read at that layer. (b) Layer 1 is a syntax-level scan that sees no receiver types and is evaded by `(OpenMode)1` or a variable argument. (c) 'The SideDb wrapper can be constructed only over a database created by the instrument' and 'only one EvidenceWriter writes files' are design intentions, not properties the scans can enforce. (d) R0 is called 'strict read-only (no side database written)', but I-2 includes optional block extents and dynamic-block reads on ReadDwgFile side databases. The host may evaluate and write anonymous blocks internally there, which no API-symbol scan sees. The repository already has a semantic Roslyn model with a DECLARED_MUTATOR classification (eng/validation/I52G3AApiCensus/Program.cs, which compiles with AutoCAD references). The design should require a semantic scan, or an IL scan that tracks constant operands, and should restate the R0 claim as 'no API write call, no save', not 'nothing is written in memory'.
minors: Table 5.4 lists 'build twice and compare hashes' under 'tests without AutoCAD'. Section 5.2 I-8 itself says the build needs the AutoCAD installation (the probe csproj uses HintPath to AcDbMgd.dll, AcMgd.dll and AcCoreMgd.dll under AutoCADInstallDir). Only the core/ library can be tested with no AutoCAD files present. 'Without a running AutoCAD' is a different claim from 'without AutoCAD'.

Root Directory.Build.props sets Deterministic, Nullable=disable and LangVersion. Root Directory.Build.targets runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and stamps SourceRevisionId into InformationalVersion, so the DLL bytes depend on the repository HEAD. The design says 'same isolation as I52Ctda' and 'deterministic compiler settings' without saying that these files are inherited. It should pin SourceRevisionId explicitly or build outside the repo tree, and state how the compile-time AutoCAD assembly versions relate to the designated machine's build.

Self-hash pinning at command start (5.1) hashes the instrument's own file and compares it with a sidecar pin in the same trusted folder.
